evidence: The original code called printValue and then execIntoBinary(binPath, [binPath, "version"], ...), so --json output would be followed by lit version's stdout on Unix or an Fprintf line on Windows. Fix 3c4c02f deleted both exec files and returns printValue directly, which removes the extra output.
guidance_note: When a command has a --json single-document contract, trace every write to stdout after the JSON print before opening the PR.

evidence: The original code was json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&m) on network JSON with no unknown-field or trailing-data check. Accepting was right. The fix's trailing check used dec.More(), which still accepts a manifest followed by a bare ']' or '}', and that came back as F13.
guidance_note: When adding a 'nothing after the document' check, use the decoder's documented EOF idiom (a second Decode must return io.EOF) rather than a method whose doc talks about elements within an array or object.

evidence: The Windows execIntoBinary dropped the Fprintf error and wrote human text regardless of --json. 3c4c02f deleted downgrade_exec_windows.go along with the F1 fix, which removes both problems instead of patching the error return.

Go's os.Rename on Windows uses MoveFileEx with MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING, so the claim that it fails whenever the target exists is wrong. The running-.exe constraint is real but unreachable: Install rejects any URL not ending in .tar.gz, and Windows archives are zip, so the agent was right not to design a Windows swap speculatively.

The original code was io.ReadAll(io.TeeReader(resp.Body, h)) with no limit. 3c4c02f added LimitReader(maxArchiveBytes+1) and an overflow check. It bounded only the compressed bytes and left the gunzip expansion unbounded, which came back as F17.
guidance_note: When bounding untrusted input at a boundary, list every stage that can grow it (download, decompress, per-entry, total) and cap each one in the same change.

evidence: Go's archive/tar Reader normalizes TypeRegA headers to TypeReg (or TypeDir) in Next(). If so, the original TypeReg-only check never rejected such archives, and the added TypeRegA branch and its test are dead. The packet does not show the Go stdlib source, so this stays unverified here.

The original loop did io.Copy(dest, tr) for every entry named lit, so two lit entries would be concatenated into one corrupted binary, even though the doc comment said 'exactly one'. 3c4c02f returns an error when a second entry appears and adds a test.
guidance_note: When a doc comment states a cardinality ('exactly one'), write the check that rejects the second occurrence in the same edit.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the tag was only checked with HasPrefix(tag, "v") in the original PR, and 3c4c02f did not touch that check. The fix was a denylist (/ \ .. whitespace) that missed ? # %, which came back as F14. Adding a resolver check while the CLI still validates the same tag creates two enforcers, not a single one.
guidance_note: When a string is interpolated into a URL, validate it with an allow-list of producer characters (or escape it with url.PathEscape) the first time, not a denylist of the characters the reviewer happened to name.

evidence: The 3c4c02f diff of downgrade.go (the F1 fix) adds a '+' blank line after the import block, which produces the double blank line. 33b4731 removed it.
guidance_note: Run gofmt on every touched Go file before pushing a review fix.

evidence: TestHTTPInstallerEnforcesSizeCap was added in 3c4c02f as part of the F5 fix. Its comment says the server streams 'maxArchiveBytes+1 bytes', but the loop writes 1 MiB chunks while written <= maxArchiveBytes. 33b4731 corrected the comment.
guidance_note: Reread each comment written in a fix against the loop or code directly beneath it before pushing.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 'var _ io.Reader = (*bytes.Reader)(nil)' and its comment are unchanged context lines in the 3c4c02f diff, so they date from the original PR. The assertion checks interface satisfaction, not double-close, and 33b4731 deleted it.
guidance_note: Delete placeholder assertions whose comment claims a guarantee the code cannot provide before opening the PR.

evidence: The F1 fix (3c4c02f) removed syscall.Exec and the Windows message path but left the PR description still describing them. The agent updated the description afterward.
guidance_note: When a review fix removes a behavior, grep the PR description and doc comments for that behavior in the same push.

evidence: Decoder.More() peeks at the next token and returns true for anything except ']' or '}', so at top level it catches a following '{' document or junk. The reviewer's '{}{}' example was already rejected, and TestHTTPResolverRejectsTrailingData (added with the More() check in 3c4c02f) was passing. The real gap is a trailing bare ']' or '}', and a second Decode requiring io.EOF closes it. The agent's reply and the ea4126f test comment claim the old check missed the two-document case and the test was a false signal, which is false.
guidance_note: Before conceding that an existing test was a false signal, revert the fix locally and run the test against the old code to see whether it actually fails.

evidence: The F8 fix (33b4731) was a denylist (ContainsAny(/ \), '..', whitespace), so ?, # and % still passed into fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/release-manifest.json"). ea4126f replaced it with the ^v[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$ allow-list. Its doc comment wrongly claimed the regex enforces semver, which came back as F24.
guidance_note: When a reviewer names some bad characters in a boundary string, replace the check with an allow-list rather than extending the denylist by the named characters.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: runDowngradeWith dates from the original PR, and its only test was normalizeDowngradeTag. 8ca685f narrowed the store dependency to schemaDowngrader, injected binPathFn, and added four pipeline tests, including the --json single-document check.
guidance_note: Ship a fake-backed test of the composed pipeline with any new command whose dependencies are already behind interfaces.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the comparison 'hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)) != a.SHA256' was in the original PR, and an uppercase digest would fail it. 8ca685f decodes the expected value up front and compares with bytes.Equal. The same reply was posted twice.
guidance_note: Compare digests as decoded bytes, never as hex strings, and validate the expected digest's length before fetching.

evidence: The F5 fix capped compressed download bytes but left io.Copy(dest, tr) streaming unbounded gunzip output, which is the same unbounded-untrusted-input gap one stage later. 2d36a94 added a header Size check and CopyN(cap+1). It still left the many-entries total unbounded, which came back as F20.
guidance_note: When capping an archive download, cap per-entry and total decompressed bytes in the same commit.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the 'Mirrors scripts/install.sh' comment was in the original PR. The 2d36a94 rewrite says the Go check is tighter because it rejects '..' and backslashes, then says install.sh 'applies the same first two checks', which contradicts itself. No reviewer caught that.
guidance_note: When a comment claims parity with another implementation, open that implementation and list the actual differences before writing the claim.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the download-then-CreateTemp order was in the original PR. 00ddb54 moved CreateTemp ahead of downloadAndVerify. That is a fail-fast ordering change and has nothing to do with dataflow versus control flow.

The F17 fix (2d36a94) checked only each entry's declared size. Non-target entries are still decompressed to reach the next header, so many entries each under the cap remained unbounded in total. 00ddb54 added boundedReader, whose '>= cap' check was off by one, which came back as F27.
guidance_note: When adding a byte cap, write the exact-at-cap and cap+1 boundary tests along with the cap.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the bare 'HTTP %d' error was in the original PR, while resolver.Resolve already included a 256-byte body snippet. 00ddb54 copied the snippet logic into the installer, which is a second copy rather than one source of truth.
guidance_note: When two fetch paths share one error shape, factor out a single helper instead of building each error ad hoc.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the map[string]string payload with fmt.Sprintf schema was in the original PR. e9c8e47 added a typed downgradeResult with Schema int64, and the test now asserts the number 3.
guidance_note: Use a typed struct for JSON output payloads from the first draft, so numbers stay numbers.

evidence: TestHTTPInstallerRejectsOversizedEntryHeader was added in 2d36a94 (the F17 fix). It builds an unused first archive with Size: 0 under a comment claiming 'far above the cap'. e9c8e47 removed the dead setup.
guidance_note: Reread a newly written test top to bottom for abandoned first attempts before pushing it.

evidence: The F14 fix (ea4126f) introduced tagAcceptPattern with a comment claiming 'goreleaser's semver-with-optional-prerelease shape', but ^v[A-Za-z0-9._+-]+$ accepts vfoo. 4d1ffe2 rewrote the comment to describe the URL-safe segment shape it actually enforces.
guidance_note: Describe a regex in its comment by what it matches, checked against a counterexample, not by what it is intended to represent.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the http.DefaultClient fallback was in the original PR, and the CLI passes context.Background(). 4d1ffe2 sets a 5-minute default Timeout. A missing deadline is not an enumeration gap in an accept/reject shape.
guidance_note: Never fall back to http.DefaultClient in code reached from a CLI with a background context. Give the default client a timeout in the first draft.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the resolver's http.DefaultClient fallback dates from the original PR and is the same gap as F25 in the sibling component. 4d1ffe2 fixed both together with a 60-second resolver default.

The boundedReader added in 00ddb54 (the F20 fix) returned errStreamCap when b.read >= b.cap, so a stream exactly cap bytes long errors instead of reaching EOF. That contradicts its own 'exceed' doc comment and the cap+1 pattern downloadAndVerify already used. f29a78c switched to cap+1 reads and added edge tests.
guidance_note: When adding a second byte cap, reuse the cap+1 idiom already in the file and test the exact-at-cap case.

evidence: Go permits slice indices of any integer type, so p[:remaining] with an int64 compiles. The same int64 slice expression p[:b.cap-b.read] had existed since 00ddb54, so the flag is a false positive: the finding is false and its subject was not new in f29a78c.

narrative: This PR took 11 Copilot rounds and 28 findings, with every push triggering a new round. About a third of the findings came from earlier fixes. The archive-cap chain (compressed cap, then per-entry cap, then total cap, then an off-by-one in the total cap) ran four rounds because each fix bounded only the stage the reviewer named. The tag-validation chain went from denylist to allow-list to a wrong comment on the allow-list. Most other late findings (timeouts, string-typed JSON, case-sensitive digest, temp-before-download) were gaps in the original PR that Copilot raised piecemeal, not fix-caused. The agent pushed back twice, both times correctly. It also accepted F13's false premise about dec.More() and wrote that false claim into a test comment.
guidance_observations: Each fix addressed exactly the instance named and stopped; sweeping the whole input-bounding surface (download, decompress per-entry, decompress total, network deadline) once would have removed four or more rounds.

Comments and doc text written inside review fixes were themselves wrong three times (F10, F23, F24, plus the uncaught F18 self-contradiction), so fix-time comments need the same check as fix-time code.
The agent conceded that an existing test was a false signal (F13) without running it against the old code, and wrote that false claim into the repo.

evidence: Adding the internal/version import makes existing locals named 'version' shadow the package in those tests. The agent renamed the two locals to appliedVersion, and round 1 raised nothing new.
guidance_note: When adding an import, grep the file for locals with the package's name and rename them in the same edit.

narrative: There was one minor shadowing finding, the agent fixed it with a variable rename, and the second round was clean. No fix caused a follow-up finding.

evidence: Re-enabling mingw/msys/cygwin left the script checking -x "$tmp/lit" and moving $tmp/lit, while Windows archives contain lit.exe. d663d82 threaded BIN_NAME through every use. It also relaxed the extracted-binary check from -x to -f, which came back as F2.
guidance_note: When rewriting a validation line during a fix, keep the original predicate (-x) unless the change requires dropping it, and say so if it does.

evidence: The d663d82 diff changes 'if [ ! -x "$tmp/lit" ]' to 'if [ ! -f "$tmp/$BIN_NAME" ]', so a non-executable POSIX extract now passes and the '|| true' version probe hides it. f91772e added chmod +x followed by a -x check. The chmod follows symlinks, which came back as F3.
guidance_note: When adding a mutating step like chmod on archive-extracted paths, reject symlinks before it.

evidence: f91772e (the F2 fix) added 'chmod +x "$tmp/$BIN_NAME"', which follows a symlink extracted by unzip and changes the target's mode, a hazard the old read-only -x test did not have. 4425164 rejects -L first.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a write to an extracted path, check the path type without following links before writing.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 4425164 flag is a false positive: 4425164 only added the -L guard and the lnks.exe removal. The missing unzip probe comes from the original PR re-enabling the zip path for Windows. 5b868bd added command -v probes for tar and unzip.
guidance_note: When re-enabling a platform, list every external tool its code path invokes and probe each one the way the existing curl/jq checks do.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT 5b868bd flag is a false positive: 5b868bd changed only install.sh, while the 'ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION || ERROR_IO_PENDING' branch in workspace_lock_windows.go was in the original PR. Treating IO_PENDING as contention would abandon a pending lock. c7f1098 surfaces it as an error.
guidance_note: When mapping OS error codes to a would-block sentinel, map only the code the API documents for that flag (ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION under LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY).

narrative: There were six rounds with one finding each. Rounds 1 and 2 were a chain: the lit.exe fix relaxed -x to -f, the chmod +x restoring executability followed symlinks, and an -L guard closed it. F4 (unzip probe) and F5 (IO_PENDING) were original-PR gaps that Copilot raised late, and their fix-commit flags are false positives. All five accepts were correct.
guidance_observations: Each fix to install.sh's extraction validation loosened or added one predicate without re-checking the whole extract-validate-install block, which produced a two-round chain.
The original-PR gaps (unzip probe, IO_PENDING) surfaced only in rounds 3 and 4, so re-enabling a platform warranted a full pass over every path that platform reaches before opening the PR.
